title: Body Sound Deadening — Mastic Patch Locations
introduction:
I use these illustrations to find the body’s butyl mastic patches: the blue areas with dashed white borders mark their locations on the floor pan, roof and front door. These patches help damp panel vibration—rather like taking the ring out of a drum skin. They are one part of the body’s noise-control materials, not a complete inventory of everything that keeps the cabin quiet.

Read each view using its panel heading. The floor-pan drawing spreads out the body floor for reference, the roof view locates patches on the roof panel, and the door view shows the patch area on the door skin. The highlighted shapes identify locations; they do not provide measured templates or installation dimensions.

For body repair involving these areas, the material sequence matters: remove nearby mastic before welding, then apply mastic before restoring corrosion protection. The notices below explain the fire and adhesion consequences. This page is a location reference with those handling requirements, not a complete welding or patch-installation procedure.

edits.text: Sound Deadeners, Insulators and Mastic Patches
edits.why: Mastic patches are part of the body’s sound-control treatment. The illustrations identify selected patch locations while other insulators and sound deadeners remain outside these views.

edits.text: NOTICE: Remove mastic from the affected area before welding there. Mastic is combustible, and heat from welding nearby can cause it to burn.
edits.why: The welding heat zone can extend beyond the weld itself, so mastic near the work area can burn even when it is not directly beneath the weld.

edits.text: NOTICE: Apply the mastic material before restoring corrosion protection to the area. Corrosion protection must be restored afterward; applying it first can reduce mastic adhesion because corrosion-protection products may be wax based.
edits.why: The order preserves the mastic’s bond to the panel while still requiring the corrosion protection to be reinstated.

edits.text: Use the illustrations to locate the butyl mastic patches. The highlighted areas are a location reference; additional insulators and sound deadeners are fitted beyond those shown.
edits.why: An unhighlighted area is not proof that it has no sound-control material. I use the drawings as a map of the identified patches, rather than a reason to overlook other insulation.
The floor-pan view marks patch areas across the floor and rear body floor. Read the blue areas against the panel shapes rather than estimating dimensions from the picture.
The roof illustration provides the roof-panel landmarks for the highlighted patch areas.
The door view places the highlighted patch area on the lower portion of the door skin.

edits.text: NOTE: The LH side is shown; the RH side has a similar arrangement.
edits.why: Use the shown left-hand door as the location reference for the similar right-hand arrangement without treating the illustration as a measured template.
